# Speculative manias

Notes after rereading accounts of old bubbles: tulips, railways, radio shares.

## Imitation

A mania is a crowd phenomenon before it is a financial one. People do not buy because they have valued the object; they buy because a neighbour or a colleague bought and got rich. Each buyer reads the other's wanting as proof that the object is worth having. The imitation spreads sideways, the wanting synchronises, and the crowd converges on one object.

## Rivalry

Late in a mania the object hardly matters. What hurts is watching a rival get rich. Envy of the neighbour does more work than greed.

## Credit

No mania without credit. The buying is done with borrowed money, which ties this to the [[Minsky moment]]. Rising prices justify the belief that made them rise: [[Reflexivity]].
